newsitem.title: USA: Thomas sees less dramatic gains ahead.
newsitem.headline: Thomas sees less dramatic gains ahead.

text.p: Thomas Industries Inc Thursday reported a 52 percent jump in profits on record first quarter sales, saying gains during the rest of the year are expected to be less dramatic.
Net income for the latest quarter was $4,002,000, or $0.37 per share, compared to $2,625,000, or $0.25 per share, in 1996.
Chief executive Timothy C. Brown noted both of the company's core business units had strong first quarters.

"Our Compressor/Vacuum Pump Group posted the highest sales and operating income for any first quarter in its history," he said, adding both the North American and European compressor segments posted strong results.

"Our Lighting Group had its strongest first quarter since 1990 in both sales and operating income, with solid performances from our Consumer, C&I Indoor and C&I Outdoor Divisions. Continued improvements from within our manufacturing operations also contributed to the Group's fine performance," he continued.

"Although we are off to a strong start, we do not anticipate the remaining nine months to show the dramatic earnings improvements experienced in the first quarter. However, we do expect the Company to show quarterly improvements in sales and earnings over 1996," Brown said.
